title: Dog Meat Reform Needs Evidence, Quarantine, and Abolition by 2030
excerpt: Rabies exposure demands urgent care, while uninspected animal transport weakens biosecurity. Vietnam needs enforceable rules—and complete abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A bite, scratch, or saliva contact with broken skin can turn an ordinary moment into a medical emergency. Rabies spreads when infected saliva reaches wounds or mucous membranes. Once symptoms appear, disease is virtually 100% fatal. World Health Organization guidance requires immediate wound washing with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, followed by urgent medical assessment for post-exposure prophylaxis.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

Claims about tradition do not answer basic safety questions: Where did each animal come from? Was transport inspected? Was quarantine enforced? Was slaughter conducted under approved food-safety controls? Without documented answers, buyers, families, and authorities cannot reliably assess disease risk or animal theft.

“Farm-raised” claims also require proof. A label cannot establish lawful origin, veterinary oversight, or safe handling. Stolen companion animals and uninspected animals moving through informal networks represent distinct harms: families lose trusted companions, while weak traceability creates biosecurity gaps. Those harms must not be hidden behind custom or unsupported assurances.

Public safety needs prevention before tragedy

Rabies prevention depends on vaccination, responsible ownership, surveillance, quarantine, and rapid treatment after exposure. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route; handling sick animals, uninspected slaughter, and bites create different risks. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains must be investigated separately, without inventing a causal link.

Vietnamese families, veterinarians, local officials, and animal-protection leaders can demand stronger enforcement together. Official rabies-control targets are not the same as SDE’s campaign demand: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for nationwide abolition by 2030, then follow campaign updates as that demand reaches decision-makers.
